# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 51 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 51 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_051_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 2 — The Elm and the Vine

**51:1** As I was walking in the countryside and observing an elm tree and a grapevine, and reflecting on them and their fruits, the Shepherd appeared to me and said: "What are you meditating on?" "Lord," I said, "I am thinking about the elm and the vine, because they are most beautiful to observe."

**51:2** "These two trees," he said, "have been set forth as a type for the servants of God." "Lord," I said, "I wish to know the type of the elm and of the vine, and what their types signify." "Do you see," he said, "the elm and the vine?" "I see them, lord," I replied.

**51:3** "This vine bears fruit," he said, "while the elm is barren. Yet this vine, unless it climbs upon the elm, cannot bear much fruit lying on the ground, and what fruit it does bear is rotten, since it is not suspended upon the elm. When therefore the vine is attached to the elm, it bears fruit both from itself and from the elm.

**51:4** "You see, then, that the elm also yields much fruit — no less than the vine, and in fact more." "How more, lord?" I asked. "Because," he said, "when the vine is suspended upon the elm, it yields much fruit, both good and beautiful; but when it lies upon the ground it yields little fruit, and that is rotten. This similitude accordingly applies to the servants of God — to the poor and to the rich."

**51:5** "How so, lord? Explain to me." "Listen," he said. "The rich man possesses wealth, yet he is poor toward the Lord, being drawn away by his riches. His prayer and confession before the Lord are small and weak and carry no power on high. But when the rich man assists the poor man and supplies his needs, believing that what he does to the poor man will find its recompense with God — for the poor man is rich in intercession and confession, and his intercession has great power before God — the rich man therefore supplies all things to the poor man without hesitation.

**51:6** The poor man, therefore, being supplied by the rich man, prays to God and gives thanks on behalf of the one who gave to him, and that rich man continues to assist the poor man diligently, so that the poor man lacks nothing in his life. For the poor man knows that the rich man cannot pray effectively, and he gives thanks to God on behalf of the rich man for what was given him. And the rich man, hearing the poor man praying on his behalf, rejoices greatly, knowing that the poor man intercedes for him before God."

**51:7** Both therefore accomplish their work: the poor man in prayer and in confession and in thanksgiving, and the rich man in the distribution of his wealth to the poor. Both therefore accomplish much before the Lord. So then, let the rich man not hesitate to give — for as he gives, the poor man intercedes for him, and through this intercession the rich man is made rich before God — nor let the poor man despise the rich man's intercession on his behalf. For both are good when they perform their respective tasks.

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and the mutual economic theology of Similitude 2.*
